cases.title: MCP: deferred tools and progressive disclosure, short descriptions first, full schemas on demand
cases.text: Make the Hypertask MCP server cheap to connect: a client should load one short line per tool at start and fetch a tool's full schema only when it is about to call it. Why now. The old objection to MCP was context bloat. Claude Code now defers tools (names first, schema on demand) and Anthropic calls that "progressive disclosure for MCPs, the same way a CLI is". Our server sends every tool's full schema and long descriptions on connect. Descriptions: first sentence under 100 characters, states what the tool returns; detail moves below a blank line so clients that truncate keep the useful part. Schemas: lean input schemas, no duplicated enums, shared $defs , output schemas declared (structured content) so clients skip parsing. Meta tools: search_tools and describe_tool for clients without native deferral (Cursor, Codex), so they can start with the meta tools only. Measure: tokens sent on connect before and after, target under 1,500 tokens for the full tool list. Parent: HTPR-6478 .

cases.title: API bug: POST /mcp/tasks/move renumbers the ticket (HTPR-5731 became HTPR-5737)
cases.text: Moving a task through the REST route changes its ticket number, which silently breaks every existing reference to that ticket. Response returns the same database id (33439) but ticketNumber HTPR-5736, and a second move produced HTPR-5737. The original index 5731 now resolves to nothing. Expected: a same-board move must never touch ticketNumber or uniqueIndex. The CLI move path preserves them correctly, so only the REST route is wrong. cases.title: Mobile: prioritize visible board data over secondary startup requests
cases.text: Make the active board win every startup request race on mobile. Secondary account, integration, preference, and navigation data should not delay visible tasks. Scope: Classify startup requests as critical, intent-driven, idle, or feature-only. Defer or cancel secondary work during board navigation and rapid board switching. Keep lightweight counts eager only when they affect the visible shell. Acceptance: The active board request starts before all secondary feature requests in a cache-disabled trace. Closed chat, unopened inbox, integrations, and settings add no competing payload. Request count and decoded bytes fall without slowing intentional inbox, chat, or board switching at p75.

cases.title: Agent token invalidated when session restarts ("Session invalidation requested")
cases.text: Gap: Managed agent tokens (JWT with agentId claim) get invalidated when the session restarts — the server returns reason: unauthorized / Session invalidation requested . The token itself has no expiry claim ( exp ), so it should outlive a session restart. Repro: Create agent token via hypertask auth login --token --agent-id <agentId> Use token in hypertask --token "$TOKEN" ... — works fine Exit session + restart Same token now returns: Session invalidation requested / reason: unauthorized Expected: A persisted agent token survives session restarts (it has no expiry). Root cause guess: Server may bind agent-session validity to a server-side session that is cleared on restart or re-auth, even though the JWT itself is still valid.

cases.title: Support HT_TOKEN env var in ht script
cases.text: Modify the ht script to check a HT_TOKEN environment variable before falling back to ~/.hypertask/config.json . This lets agents switch between user identity and agent identity per session without mutating the config file. Gap Currently ht always reads ~/.hypertask/config.json . To use an agent bearer token (e.g. one with an agentId claim), you must either edit the config file or use the slower hypertask --token CLI — ht has no token override mechanism. Fix Add an HT_TOKEN env var check at the top of ~/.local/bin/ht , before reading config. If set, use it instead of the saved token. The ht script is a ~4x faster alternative to the full CLI (skips Node startup), so it's the natural path for agent token use. Usage HT_TOKEN=$AGENT_TOKEN ht GET /mcp/tasks?ticket_number=HTPR-3976

In plain English: the sidebar starts with a placeholder empty list of boards. React Query was told that placeholder counts as data that was just fetched, and separately told to trust fresh data for a minute. So it concludes it already has an up-to-date board list, and never asks the server. You get an empty sidebar that looks exactly like your boards were deleted. Evidence (headless, live production, userId 6). Instrumented XHR and fetch before opening the switcher, then opened it: calls: [] , groups: 1 . Zero network requests to /api/teams/getAllSidebar . The endpoint itself is fine: called by hand from the same page it returns 200 with 12 teams and 30 boards . The persisted cache held {status: "success", data: [], dataUpdatedAt: 2 hours old} and was still never refetched. Cause: in useGetAllTeamsMinimal ,...

cases.title: CLI can create a task relation but cannot list or remove one
cases.text: The CLI can link two tasks but gives you no way to see existing links or undo one, so a wrong link is unfixable from the terminal. hypertask tasks link <source> <target> --type RelatedTo creates a relation. There is no list and no unlink . The REST API has had all three for months: GET , POST and DELETE on /mcp/tasks/relations . Now unblocked. Those routes previously demanded an internal database id or a ticket number and refused unique_index + project_id . HTPR-5159 fixed that, so the CLI can pass whatever identifier the user typed. Proposed: hypertask tasks relations <ticket> lists relations both directions, showing type and the other ticket hypertask tasks unlink <source> <target> [--type] removes one Correcting the parity matrix while I am here: HTPR-4834 lists "task relations entirely" and "related and next-task suggestions" as missing from the CLI. That is out of date: tasks link , tasks related and tasks next all exist and work. List and unlink are the only real gaps.

cases.title: Agent assignees are invisible on every read path (tasks list agent=null, /mcp/tasks reports them as userId 6)
cases.text: No read endpoint tells you which agents own a ticket, so agent ownership cannot be audited or corrected. This blocks the Board Maintainer's job of resolving ownership conflicts. In plain English: you can assign an agent to a ticket, but you cannot then ask the API who owns it. The answer comes back either empty or as Valentin's user id. hypertask tasks list --project 15 --json returns agent: null for tickets that provably have agent assignees. cases.title: AI chat: add project_admin so the chat can archive, restore and invite to boards
cases.text: The chat cannot archive a board, restore one, or invite a person or agent, though MCP callers can. So board administration is only reachable from the surface most users never touch. What to build: a chat tool mirroring the MCP project_admin tool, which archives or restores an owned board and invites a human or agent to an accessible board. Read and write the same rows the MCP route writes, behind the same access checks: archiving is owner-only, inviting requires board access. Do not call the mcp-server service layer from the chat route. Those services are HTTP clients that request this same app, which makes the chat mint a credential and call itself. Use the underlying controllers directly, as the other chat tools do. Fourth item from the surface parity audit on HTPR-4834 .

cases.title: setTaskLabels deletes labels without recording removal activity, so data loss is silent
cases.text: setTaskLabels wipes a task’s labels with a bare deleteMany and records nothing, so a destructive label write leaves no trace in history. In src/lib/mcp/tasks/services.ts : it calls prisma.taskLabel.deleteMany({ where: { taskId } }) , then creates the new labels and fires createLabelActivity only for those. Every removed label vanishes with no activity row. Real damage, tonight. A bulk update through --labels replaced rather than added, destroying every other label on ~90 tickets. Nothing in the UI or the history showed it had happened. I recovered 75 labels across 36 tickets by replaying the original additions , which is only possible because those were logged. Had any of those labels been removed by this same path earlier, they would be unrecoverable. Two asks: Log removals. Emit a TaskLabel activity with a removed status for each label deleteMany drops, so the feed tells the truth and a bad write is recoverable. Consider making the additive path the default. mutateTaskLabels already...

cases.title: tasks list --label silently drops a task that carries the label
cases.text: A task with the filtered label does not appear in the filtered list, so anything driving work off that filter silently misses tickets. Reproduced on production, 2026-08-06, twice in a row with identical output: hypertask tasks list --project 15 --label "📲MOBILE" --limit 100 returns 9 rows . HTPR-4116 is not among them, yet tasks get HTPR-4116 shows Labels 📲MOBILE, Calendar 📅 . It was present in the same query earlier today, before it gained a second label and a second assignee entry. Two things to check: whether the label filter breaks on tasks carrying more than one label, and whether the duplicated assignee row on that task (it lists Valentin Yeo, Valentin Yeo ) is joining the query into dropping it. Why it matters beyond one ticket: agent tooling uses this filter as its work queue, so a dropped row is invisible work, not a cosmetic gap.

cases.title: Comment composer has no in-flight guard, so two fast sends post two comments
cases.text: Pressing send twice before the first request lands posts the comment twice. Nothing blocks the second press. No flag: sendComment and the Ctrl+Enter branch in TipTapTaskDetail.tsx call handleCallback with no isPending check. No disabled state: the send button in TiptapMainContainer.tsx is never disabled while a send is in flight. Each press queues its own upload with a fresh Date.now() id, so the per-upload guard in UploadingCommentContainer does not catch it. That guard only stops one upload posting twice. Fix: a single in-flight flag that both the keyboard path and the button respect, cleared when the comment lands or fails. Split out of HTPR-3175 , whose wrong-task half is fixed in PR #2337 .

cases.title: No way to read a project's labels: GET /mcp/labels 404s and the CLI has no list command
cases.text: Labels can be created and applied, but never listed. The only way an agent discovers what labels exist is by deliberately applying a wrong one and reading the error message. What fails: ht GET "/mcp/labels?project_id=15" returns {"error":"not found"} . The route does not exist. hypertask labels list --project 15 and hypertask label list --project 15 both return unknown command . There is no read subcommand, only project label create . The workaround that actually works , which is the tell: hypertask tasks update HTPR-5015 --labels "does not exist" fails with a message listing all 48 labels in the project. So the data is there, it is just only reachable through a failure path. Expected: a GET /mcp/labels?project_id=<id> that returns the label list, and a hypertask labels list --project <id> that wraps it. Why it matters: every agent that tags its own tickets has to either hardcode label names or trigger an error on purpose to read them.

cases.title: CLI bug: tasks assign/unassign cannot target an agent, and task_id silently hits the wrong task
cases.text: Two gaps found while wiring an agent identity to board 15 tickets. The CLI cannot assign an agent. hypertask tasks assign HTPR-5037 --assignee <agent-uuid> fails with Either user_id, (user_ids + mode: 'multiple'), or assign_self must be provided . The API supports assign_self and the agent token carries the agentId, but the CLI exposes no way to reach it. Same for tasks unassign . Workaround is a raw POST to /api/mcp/assignees/assign . /api/mcp/assignees/assign accepts task_id as an internal id with no board check. Passing task_id: 3127 while intending ticket HTPR-3127 (internal id 21769) assigned the agent to an unrelated task on a different board, and returned success. The agent token is scoped to project 15 only, so that write should have been refused. Prefer project_id + unique_index , but the access check is the real fix. Wrong assignment was reverted with intent: "unassign" .

cases.title: A team whose card fails keeps full premium access indefinitely
cases.text: In plain English: you said a team whose card is blocked should lose premium. Right now they do not. They keep everything, forever, while paying nothing. Found while shipping HTPR-4216 . You described the intended model as: anyone can join a team, and if the payer's card fails the team drops off premium. The first half is now true. The second half was never implemented. What the code actually does : the plan gate treats only Expired , ended and canceled as dead ( src/app/api/ai/_lib/planGate.ts:11 , mirrored in src/lib/deriveCurrentBoardBilling.ts ). Stripe's past_due and unpaid are not in that list, so a failed-payment team still resolves to Pro and keeps every premium feature. This is not hypothetical : a client sat on a past_due subscription with full access, which is part of what HTPR-4153 untangled. Why it matters more now : seat billing no longer blocks anyone at the door, deliberately, because the joiner is not the payer. That is the right call, but it means the payment gate has...

cases.title: Two people joining a team at the same time can lose a paid seat
cases.text: In plain English: if two people accept invites to the same team within a second of each other, Stripe can end up billing for one seat fewer than the team actually has. We keep serving the extra person for free until someone else joins. Not urgent, and not caused by the seat-billing fix in HTPR-4216 . It predates it. Surfaced by the review on PR #2181 . Why it happens : seat sync reads the current Stripe quantity, works out the new one, then writes it. Those are three separate steps with no lock. Two joins landing together both read the same starting number, and the write that lands last wins, even if it was calculated from the staler read. What makes it worse : the Member_Team table has no unique constraint on user plus team, so the same person joining twice concurrently can create two membership rows and double-count the seats. It partly self-heals : the next person to join recalculates from real membership and charges the whole gap. So the loss is temporary on an active team, and...

cases.title: Turn on real-user speed tracking (PostHog web vitals) - we're flying blind on how fast the app feels
cases.text: We have no data on how fast the app actually feels to real users. PostHog can tell us, but the setting is off. In plain English: all our speed numbers today come from a robot loading one page on a test connection. That tells us nothing about what real people on real phones experience. PostHog already runs on the site and can measure it from actual visits, but the performance setting was never switched on. PostHog itself flags it: "Performance monitoring setup: 0/1 passed." Why it matters: one of the four measurements, INP (how quickly the app responds when you click or type), cannot be measured by a robot at all . It only exists from real usage. So right now we are completely blind to how responsive the app feels, which is exactly the thing people notice most. The fix: add capture_performance: { web_vitals: true } to the PostHog setup in PostHogAnalytics.tsx . Three lines. It then reports LCP, CLS, FCP and INP from real sessions. cases.title: N+1 detector: log requests that issue too many Prisma queries
cases.text: Add a ~20-line Prisma middleware that logs any request issuing more than ~10 queries, so N+1 fan-outs surface in logs before users hit pool exhaustion. In plain English The HTPR-4033 bug (opening a task fired one database write per comment) ran in production for weeks and was only noticed when Sentry caught users hitting errors. A tiny counter inside the app would have flagged that route on day one, before any user felt it. Why it is worth building Catches this whole bug class proactively - any future route that loops database calls per item gets named in the logs immediately. Nearly free - ~20 lines, no new dependency, negligible overhead. Technical sketch Extend the Prisma client in src/lib/prisma.ts with $extends : count queries per request (AsyncLocalStorage keyed per invocation), and console.warn route + count when a request exceeds a threshold (~10). Warnings land in Vercel function logs; optionally also Sentry as a non-error event. Keep it log-only - no blocking, no throwing.

cases.title: CLI bug: tasks create silently exits with no output when --labels value does not match an existing label
cases.text: The CLI exits successfully with zero output when --labels is given a non-matching label, so the ticket is never created and the caller believes it worked. Command that failed silently: hypertask tasks create --project 15 --title "..." --labels "BUG woodlouse-emoji" --assignee 6 --description "..." Result: no stdout, no stderr, exit status looked fine, and no task existed afterwards (confirmed by searching). Re-running the identical command without --labels created the ticket immediately ( HTPR-4690 ). Expected: either create the task and ignore or create the unknown label, or fail loudly with a non-zero exit and a message naming the invalid label and listing valid ones. Silent success is the worst outcome because automation cannot detect it.
